input.quote: provided that either Party may make such an assignment without the other Party's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 13.4.1 secures our side of the preferred position (we may assign to an Affiliate or a merger/stock/asset successor without consent, and consent to other assignments is expressly not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and no provision gives Harpoon any termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie Change of Control (Article 12 gives Harpoon only breach and insolvency terminations; Section 13.2 deals solely with a Harpoon Change in Control and confers rights on us). It does not, however, sit at fallback either: the mutual no-consent exception lets Harpoon assign the Agreement to any Affiliate or successor — including one owned by a competitor — with no consent, no notice and no competitor bar. We therefore limit the no-consent exception to AbbVie and add an absolute prohibition on assignment by Harpoon to a Competitor, leaving the existing reasonableness standard and the affiliate-responsibility, binding-effect and assumption mechanics untouched.

proposal.summary: Limit the no-consent assignment exception to AbbVie and bar Harpoon from assigning to a Competitor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We keep our right to assign to an Affiliate or successor without consent, but Harpoon's assignments should require our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, as Section 13.4.1 already provides) and should never be made to a Competitor. Happy to discuss a notice-based mechanic for Harpoon successor assignments as a fallback.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
mappings.quote: Without the prior written consent of the other Party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, neither Party shall sell, transfer, assign, delegate, pledge, or otherwise dispose of, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder

mappings.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
